request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both surfaces of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty on the request and list only the veterinarians holding it, matched on the whole name and case-insensitively. A blank or absent value lists everyone; a specialty nobody holds lists no one. Paging keeps the specialty. Neither surface gains a reader-facing control.
acceptance_criteria: The veterinarian page accepts an optional specialty query parameter and lists only the veterinarians holding the named specialty.
The machine-readable veterinarian list accepts the same optional parameter and returns only the veterinarians holding the named specialty.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and disregards letter case; a name that is only part of a stored specialty matches nothing.
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is listed whenever any one of them is named.
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns the normal page or document, successfully, with no veterinarian listed.
An empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves as if the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search.
Without the parameter, both surfaces behave exactly as they did before this slice.
Page-turning links on a narrowed page carry the named specialty, so every page of the narrowed directory stays reachable.
Page and item counts on a narrowed page describe the narrowed directory, not the whole one.
Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other control for choosing a specialty.
non_goals: Free-text search for a veterinarian by name — the unchanged half of NG-9 keeps it out.
Searching for a pet or a visit.
A reader-facing filter control (form, dropdown, link) on either surface; the owner deferred it to a possible later request.
Narrowing by more than one specialty at a time.
Narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty.
Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application — NG-2 stands.
Removing or reusing the withdrawn id REQ-VET-002.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and adds no type, layer, or dependency: narrowing is a repository concern, and the controller only binds and delegates. VetRepository gains a pair of whole-name, case-insensitive, distinct derived queries mirroring the existing findAll() / findAll(Pageable) pair, one per surface of the Veterinarian directory. VetController normalizes the parameter at the web boundary (strip; blank reads the whole directory) on the precedent of OwnerController's empty owner search, and exposes the normalized value so the page links carry it. New ground recorded this dispatch: narrowed reads bypass the vets cache (docs/adr/2026-08-17-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-reads.md), and case folding happens in the query rather than via column collation (system-design.md Persistence). Contracts rows for VetRepository, VetController and Vets now carry REQ-VET-003 — Vets replaces its em dash, since the machine-readable surface is supported again. The Known Defects row calling that route requirement-less is removed, matching PRD edge case 2.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two narrowed reads — one paged for the HTML page, one unpaged for the machine-readable surface — matching on the whole specialty name, ignoring case, distinct per veterinarian. Neither carries @Cacheable.

VetController's two handlers each take an optional specialty parameter, strip it, and treat blank as absent; the whole-directory path keeps calling the cached methods, so REQ-VET-001 is byte-for-byte unchanged.

vetList.html page links carry the specialty; the controller adds the normalized value to the model solely so the links can be built. No form, dropdown, or link for choosing a specialty is added (AC 10).
Page and item counts come from the narrowed Page, so they describe the narrowed directory (AC 9).
The vets cache is untouched: no new cache name, no eviction change, no new @Cacheable method.

patterns.description: blank-to-broadest normalization at the web boundary — the precedent the blank specialty follows (strip, then treat empty as no filter)
derived paged query over a filtered collection; the narrowed vet query is the same shape, traversing Vet.specialties.name with the IgnoreCase and Distinct keywords
existing pagination helper; extend it with the specialty rather than adding a second helper
page links use string preprocessing today; the narrowed links need Thymeleaf's parameterized link form @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=...)}, which URL-encodes the caller's value
@DataJpaTest against the real H2 seed data — the home for the matching-semantics tests; seeded vet 3 holds two specialties, which covers the multi-specialty criterion

risks.risk: VetControllerTests mocks VetRepository, so the case-insensitive, whole-name and multi-specialty criteria would be asserted against a stub and prove nothing about the query.
risks.mitigation: Assert matching semantics in ClinicServiceTests against the real database and seed data; keep the MockMvc tests for parameter binding, model contents, counts and page links.

risks.risk: Building the page link by string concatenation would emit the caller's raw value into the href, breaking the link for a value containing a space or an ampersand.
risks.mitigation: Use the parameterized link expression, which URL-encodes each parameter; Thymeleaf's default output escaping stays on for the rendered attribute.

risks.risk: The specialties table has a plain index, not a unique one, so a join on the specialty name could list a veterinarian twice and corrupt the page counts.
risks.mitigation: Use the Distinct keyword in the derived query name.

risks.risk: Caching the narrowed query would key an unevictable cache on an attacker-supplied string, since every route is open.
risks.mitigation: Declined by ADR 2026-08-17-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-reads; the narrowed reads query the database each time.

risks.risk: An explicit JOIN FETCH over the eager many-to-many would force Hibernate to paginate in memory.
risks.mitigation: Keep the plain derived query returning a Page, exactly as the existing findAll(Pageable) does.

risks.risk: Pre-existing and out of scope: the cached paged read is keyed by the caller-supplied page number, and a page of 0 or less makes PageRequest.of throw into the error page.
risks.mitigation: Do not fix in this slice — no acceptance criterion covers it. Recorded in system-design.md Open Questions item 5 so it is not lost.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. | Verdict is new rather than minor because the interaction between a caller-supplied filter key and the project's one unevictable cache is design ground durable memory did not cover; it is recorded as an ADR, since .scratch is not durable. | Docs written this dispatch: docs/system-design.md (provenance clause, Contracts invariants paragraph, three Contracts rows, Persistence, Known Defects row removed, Open Question 5), docs/adr/2026-08-17-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-reads.md (new), docs/adr/README.md (index rows for both 2026-08-17 ADRs — the product expert's non-goal ADR row is the flagged follow-up, now closed). | Open question recorded rather than consulted, per the owner's standing instruction: whether narrowed reads should join the cache once eviction and a size limit are settled — recorded in the ADR's Consequences and tied to system-design.md Open Questions item 5. | Ubiquitous language: prose says Veterinarian directory and Specialty; vet and specialty stay as code symbols.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain, not verified against the NVD: no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured, and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran in this review. The change adds and modifies no dependency — build.gradle and gradle/ are outside the change set — so the resolved artifact set is byte-for-byte the pre-slice set (Spring Boot 4.1.0, io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7, javaformat 0.0.47, nohttp 0.0.11, CycloneDX 3.2.4). Closing the check against the NVD is a standing CI/human task for the project, not work this slice introduced.

Template readability, no exploit path: vetList.html:20 binds a row-local th:each variable also named specialty, which shadows the new model attribute of that name inside the vet table body. The paging links sit outside that element so today's rendering is correct, but a later edit inside the table that reaches for ${specialty} would silently pick up the row-local binding. Renaming the loop variable (for example to vetSpecialty) would remove the ambiguity. Raised for the code-quality reviewer's judgment; it buys no cycle here.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty reaches the database only through two Spring Data derived queries (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, paged and unpaged) whose criteria are bound parameters. No string-concatenated query text, no JPQL/native fragment, no Sort or property name derived from the request. Meets the security-principles.md 'Injection into data access' row.

Cross-site scripting: the caller-supplied specialty is never rendered as text and never enters a th:utext. It reaches the page only as a link-expression parameter, @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value before Thymeleaf's default attribute escaping applies. Verified by the regression test asserting specialty=small%20%26%20exotic. The change additionally removes five __${...}__ preprocessing usages from vetList.html, so this template no longer builds any href by expression preprocessing — a net reduction of the template-injection surface. Swept the remaining preprocessing sites (fragments/inputField.html, fragments/selectField.html, fragments/layout.html, owners/ownersList.html, owners/ownerDetails.html); all are pre-existing, fed by entity identifiers and fragment-local names, not by request text, and all are outside this change set.

Cache poisoning and unbounded cache growth: neither narrowed read carries @Cacheable, so an attacker-supplied string never becomes a key in the unevictable, size-unlimited vets cache. The whole-directory path still calls the cached findAll methods, so REQ-VET-001's behavior is unchanged. The reasoning is recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-17-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-reads.md and repeated in the VetRepository Javadoc, so a reader who copies this code inherits the reasoning. The resulting per-request database read matches how OwnerController's caller-supplied last-name search already behaves, so the pattern is consistent with the neighboring implementation.

Boundary validation and fail-secure defaults: normalizedSpecialty strips and maps blank to null at the web boundary, following OwnerController's empty-search precedent; the null branch is the pre-existing whole-directory read, so an absent or degenerate value degrades to the prior behavior rather than to an unfiltered query built from empty text. Query-string length is bounded by the container's request-header limit, so no unbounded allocation is reachable through the parameter. Page size stays the fixed 5.

No new exposed surface: both handlers are pre-existing routes gaining an optional parameter; no route, no management endpoint, no binder, and no dependency is added. No mutable state is added to the singleton controller — normalizedSpecialty and findVets are pure. No logging, no file, process, network, reflection, or deserialization path is touched, so the log-injection, path-traversal, unsafe-deserialization and credential-disclosure classes are not engaged. Scanned the whole change set for credentials: the only hits are pre-existing descriptive prose in docs/system-design.md's Security Context and Threat Model, not values.

Error and information disclosure: no new exception is constructed or message composed, so nothing new can reach the error page that already renders exception text (system-design.md Known Defects). A specialty nobody holds returns an ordinary empty 200 on both surfaces rather than an error, asserted on both surfaces.

author: code-quality-reviewer
recommendations: src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html:36-60 repeats the same '${specialty == null} ? @{...(page=X)} : @{...(page=X,specialty=${specialty})}' ternary five times, once per page link. The duplication is justified (Thymeleaf writes a null @{} parameter as an empty 'specialty=', confirmed against Thymeleaf's documented behavior), and it extends the template's pre-existing per-link repetition rather than introducing a new pattern, so it is not blocking. A th:with-computed pair of query-string fragments, or a small link-building fragment, would let a future edit change the five hrefs in one place instead of five.

recommendations: The unvalidated page parameter is a real, pre-existing availability concern that this delta documents but does not close: an unauthenticated caller can drive PageRequest.of into IllegalArgumentException with ?page=0, and can mint an unbounded number of distinct keys in the size-limited-by-nothing `vets` cache with ?page=1..N. It is out of REQ-VET-003's scope and now correctly recorded as an owner decision in Open Questions item 5; it merits its own slice (bind the parameter with a lower bound and configure a cache size limit or eviction).

Supply chain was not re-verified this round: the delta touches no build file, and the round-1 position stands — the OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is not configured, so no NVD match has run in any review of this slice. A human or CI still owes that check.

The correction increases operational honesty about a pre-existing gap rather than introducing surface: no new input, boundary, sink, dependency, or credential handling appears in the delta.
No secrets, tokens, credentials, hostnames, or internal identifiers are disclosed by the added prose; it names only behaviour already visible in the committed source.

summary: narrow both vet directory surfaces by specialty

blast_radius.note: Eleven files but one module: two new derived reads on VetRepository, an optional parameter on each of the two existing vet handlers, and one template. No sensitive paths, no build or config file, no schema change. The template rewrite does touch the unnarrowed page, since all five paging links move off string preprocessing to the parameterized link form, but both handlers fall through to the pre-existing cached findAll when no specialty is named, so REQ-VET-001 behavior is unchanged by construction. semantic_surprise.note: I read every production hunk against its description and found no divergence. normalizedSpecialty strips and maps blank to null, following the OwnerController precedent, and the null branch is literally the old call; page and item counts come from the narrowed Page, so they describe the narrowed list; the link ternary omits the parameter entirely when none was named, since Thymeleaf would otherwise emit a bare empty specialty parameter. One latent trap, correct today and worth a human eye: vetList.html line 20 binds a row-local th:each variable also named specialty, shadowing the new model attribute of the same name inside the table body. The paging links sit outside that element, so rendering is right, but a later edit inside the table reaching for that name would silently pick up the row value. The security reviewer raised it as a recommendation and it was left unrenamed.

test_adequacy.note: The tests exercise the behavior rather than restate it, and they are split correctly: matching semantics (whole-name, case-folding, partial-name non-match, nobody-holds, multi-specialty vet, narrowed paging counts) live in ClinicServiceTests as a DataJpaTest against the real H2 seed data, so the derived query itself is proven; the mocked MockMvc tests confine themselves to binding, model attributes, counts and rendered links. Negative assertions are present (a narrowed page must not contain the excluded vet), the URL-encoding of a value carrying a space and an ampersand is asserted against the rendered href, and the no-reader-control criterion is asserted as the absence of form and select elements. These would fail against a broken implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: The roster approved, but not silently. The doc-reviewer requested changes in round 1 (system-design item 5 did not record the risk the design-block claimed it recorded) and approved only after the fix. Every other approval carries recommendations, and two are substantive rather than polish: the security reviewer's round-2 approval records that an unauthenticated caller can drive PageRequest.of into an IllegalArgumentException with a page of 0, and can mint unbounded keys in the size-unlimited vets cache by walking page numbers, pre-existing and out of this slice's scope, now documented but not closed; and that no supply-chain check ran against the NVD in either round because no Dependency-Check plugin is configured. Both are handed to a human or to CI, not resolved here.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the owner's intake decision closely, including the parts that move product scope: the NG-9 narrowing recorded as a row edit plus a non-goal ADR (the NG-4/NG-5 precedent), the machine-readable surface reinstated under a fresh id with REQ-VET-002 left withdrawn and unreused, and no reader-facing control on either surface. No consultations, no build retries against the current design record, and the single design revision was a documentation-prose fix, not a change of shape. The one judgment call, a single requirement id covering both the filter and the reinstated JSON surface, is taken as the narrowest reading and recorded as an open question, exactly as the owner instructed.

rationale: The code reads clean at every flagged coordinate and the tests prove the query, not the stub. What deserves attention is what the reviewers parked: a page number of 0 still throws into the error page on both vet surfaces, the vets cache still has no size limit, and no dependency scan has run. Also decide whether to rename the row-local specialty variable in vetList.html before someone trips over the shadowing.
